query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases and why catastrophic failure may occur? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, predicted observations relative to the starting-state baseline, applicable exposure boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The degradation of additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases is governed by the formation of a brittle oxide scale at the grain boundaries, leading to a reduction in ductility and ultimately catastrophic failure.
generation.material_initial_state: Additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix
generation.intervention: Controlled exposure to oxidizing (air) or reducing (argon-4% hydrogen) gases at 800°C for 100 hours
generation.conditions: Temperature: 800°C, Time: 100 hours, Gas composition: air or argon-4% hydrogen
generation.mechanism: Formation of a brittle oxide scale at the grain boundaries, reducing ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% reduction in tensile ductility relative to the starting-state baseline
generation.baseline: Tensile ductility of the as-manufactured alloy
generation.uncertainty: The exact composition and structure of the oxide scale may vary depending on the specific gas composition and exposure conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled gas exposure experiment with microstructure analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the tensile ductility reduction is less than 20% after exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases, the hypothesis is falsified
